data.long_meaning: The name Justyn is derived from the Greek name Ioustinos, which means 'upholder of law, just, righteous'. In the Christian context, the name symbolizes faith, morality, and righteousness. The name Justyn carries the meaning “Righteous, Just” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Justyn usually hope their child will grow to embody righteous, just and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Justyn Martyr (AD 100-165): An early Christian apologist and philosopher. He wrote the first surviving Syriac apologies for Christianity, including the second-century work 'First Apology'. He was a contemporary of Marcus Aurelius and Lucian of Samosata, and wrote in defense of Christianity against Roman criticisms.
historical_references.context: Defence of Christianity against Roman criticisms

historical_references.reference: Justyn Populus (d. AD 523): A bishop of Rome, known for his role in the disputes between the Oriental and Western Churches. He is also remembered for his efforts to secure the freedom of the Roman See from the Byzantine Emperor Justin I. His pontificate is noted for the Council of the Five Hundred, which was the last major ecumenical council before the Great Schism.
